About the Respiratory Therapy event

Respiratory Therapy is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Respiratory Therapy 2026–27 test plan (foundations, assessment, cardiopulmonary diseases and basic therapeutics 20% each; applied anatomy and physiology and patient education 10% each) and all seven Round Two skills, built around Egan’s Fundamentals of Respiratory Care, DHO: Health Science and AARC resources. Includes labeled airway diagrams, breath-sound and ABG drills, oxygen-device comparisons, a vitals report lab, Apgar practice and step-ordering for every rating sheet. Always follow the scenario and rating sheets you are given.

Sample Respiratory Therapy questions

1. Which stimulus most strongly drives breathing in a healthy person?

  1. A fall in arterial oxygen
  2. A rise in arterial carbon dioxide
  3. A rise in blood glucose
  4. A fall in body temperature
Show answer

B. A rise in arterial carbon dioxide

Central chemoreceptors respond to changes in CO₂ and pH in the cerebrospinal fluid. The hypoxic drive becomes more important in some chronic CO₂ retainers.

2. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is classified as which type of lung disease?

  1. Restrictive
  2. Obstructive
  3. Reversible
  4. Infectious
Show answer

A. Restrictive

Scarring stiffens the lungs and reduces lung volumes, a restrictive pattern. Patients often have fine crackles and clubbing.

3. Fever and acidosis shift the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to the right. What does this mean?

  1. Hemoglobin releases oxygen to tissues more easily
  2. Hemoglobin holds on to oxygen more tightly
  3. The blood carries no oxygen
  4. Carbon dioxide cannot leave the blood
Show answer

A. Hemoglobin releases oxygen to tissues more easily

A right shift lowers hemoglobin’s affinity for oxygen, so more oxygen is unloaded in active, warm, acidic tissues.
